title: Optical land-cover analysis
query: What land cover types are present in this scene?
answer: The scene is predominantly bare soil (69% of classified pixels). Class breakdown: bare soil 69%, vegetation 23%, water 4%.

title: Text-guided region grounding
answer: Found 3 distinct water regions, covering about 1.16 km² (11572 px). Each region is one connected patch of water mapped at about 10 m per pixel.

title: Grounding with a withheld count
answer: The built up extent is mapped (covering about 1.13 km² (11305 px)), but the number of separate regions cannot be stated reliably from this image alone. Each region is one connected patch of built-up land mapped at about 10 m per pixel — a block of development, not an individual building. Structures closer together than the pixel size cannot be separated.

title: SAR backscatter analysis
query: Describe the SAR backscatter in this image.
answer: The VV radar backscatter is predominantly diffuse scattering (92% of valid pixels, mean -13.0 dB). Regimes separated: smooth, diffuse, double bounce. Diffuse scattering is consistent with vegetation, bare soil, rough natural terrain — radar cannot decide between these from backscatter alone.

title: Optical + SAR fusion
query: Combine the optical and radar images to map land cover.
answer: Combining optical and radar evidence, the scene is predominantly bare soil (70% of classified pixels). Both sensors independently agree on 98% of the classified area. The largest sensor disagreement (1.4% of the scene) was resolved by radar in favour of bare soil.

title: Bi-temporal change analysis
query: What changed between the two dates?
answer: Change was detected across 10.7% of the valid area (about 2.81 km²). The dominant transition is bare soil to vegetation, covering 33% of the changed area. 66% of the detected change is corroborated by both detectors.
